The first confirmed exoplanets were indeed discovered orbiting the pulsar PSR B1257+12 in the constellation Virgo, approximately 2,300 light-years from Earth. These planets, designated PSR B1257+12 b and PSR B1257+12 c (with a third planet PSR B1257+12 d also confirmed), were discovered by Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail in 1992. This discovery was groundbreaking as it provided the first definitive proof of planets existing outside our solar system. The detection was made possible by observing tiny variations in the pulsar's radio pulse timing caused by the gravitational influence of the orbiting planets.
